subject.title: [Bug]: unresolvable compaction model reports reason=unknown — the one bucket the mid-turn precheck treats as fatal, so a config error kills the session

question: For a session model owned by a non-embedded harness and no explicit compaction model, should OpenClaw select a supported embedded target automatically, require a configured compaction target with startup/Doctor diagnostics, or delegate compaction to that harness?
rationale: The current fallback to the session model is an established tested behavior, while changing it affects model routing, startup diagnostics, and existing configurations; source inspection cannot establish the intended compatibility contract alone.

options.title: Require and diagnose a compatible target
options.body: Keep the current fallback contract only where it is executable, otherwise fail early with a precise startup/Doctor repair path for `agents.defaults.compaction.model`.

options.title: Choose an embedded default automatically
options.body: Select a known embedded-capable default when the session model belongs to a non-embedded harness, accepting a new implicit model-routing policy.

options.title: Add harness-owned compaction
options.body: Have each applicable agent harness provide compaction so its session model never crosses into the embedded runtime.

recommendation.title: Require and diagnose a compatible target
recommendation.body: Keep the current fallback contract only where it is executable, otherwise fail early with a precise startup/Doctor repair path for `agents.defaults.compaction.model`.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the precheck recovery path whose compatibility and user-visible failure semantics need to be defined.
